title: Chalé Sauce with Roasted Peppers
author: Zoe Adjei
desc: The later printing — six hundred grams of fresh tomato and two roasted red peppers, simmered until the tomato tartness diminishes.
longDesc: The same sauce as printed three years later, and it has changed substantially. The fresh tomato option more than doubles, from two hundred and fifty grams to six hundred; two roasted red bell peppers appear, which were not there before; and the chilli flakes drop from a tablespoon to half a teaspoon. The roasted peppers make it rounder and sweeter — closer to the pepper-forward bases used across West Africa and further from a straight tomato sauce. The cue is unchanged and still the best part: simmer thirty-five to forty minutes until the tomato tartness diminishes.
ingredients: 400 g tin tomatoes, or 600 g fresh tomatoes
5 cm piece fresh root ginger, grated
1 small red scotch bonnet chilli — use half and deseed it if you have a low heat tolerance
1/2 tsp dried chilli flakes — see the note on the missing unit
equipment: Grill or oven, for the peppers
steps: Roast the red bell peppers and remove the skins.
Blend the tomatoes, roasted peppers, tomato purée, onion, ginger, scotch bonnet, chilli flakes, garlic and salt to a fairly smooth paste.
// This is the uncooked chalé sauce.
To cook it: heat the oil and sauté the finely diced onion until softened.
Add the curry powder and extra-hot chilli powder.
Simmer 35 to 40 minutes, until the tomato tartness diminishes.
chefTips: Roast the peppers properly and skin them. Raw red pepper blended in gives a thin, vegetal note; roasted gives the sweetness this version is reaching for.
Until the tomato tartness diminishes, same as the earlier printing. Thirty-five to forty minutes and taste rather than watch.
The heat guidance is the author's own and worth following: use half the scotch bonnet and deseed it if your tolerance is low.
Six hundred grams of fresh tomato against two hundred and fifty in the earlier printing. If you have made the old version, this will taste noticeably milder and fuller.
Half a teaspoon of chilli flakes, down from a tablespoon. With the extra-hot chilli powder still at a teaspoon in the cooking stage, the total heat is similar but less raw.
One printing of this version omits salt from the list entirely while another includes it to taste. Salt it — the earlier printing used a full teaspoon.
Use it anywhere the earlier version is called for. The volumes are the same even though the composition is not.
commonMistakes: Leaving the salt out because one printing omits it.
A whole undeseeded scotch bonnet if you are heat-sensitive.
Treating this and the 2017 version as interchangeable in flavour.
sources: Adapted from 'Chalé Sauce', taste.co.za. BYLINE AS PRINTED: 'By Zoe Adjonyoh'. Date printed: '23 March 2020'. CREDIT AS PRINTED: 'Extract from Zoe's Ghana Kitchen... published by Octopus Publishing Group'. Yield as printed: 'Makes 500 ml'. Quantities confirmed across two fetches (TWO-PASS).

Ingredients exactly as printed: 400 g can tomatoes or 600 g fresh tomatoes; 2 roasted red bell peppers; 30 g tomato purée; 1 small white onion, roughly diced; 5 cm piece fresh root ginger, grated; 1 small red Scotch Bonnet chilli (use half and de-seed if you have a low heat tolerance); '½ dried chilli flakes'; 3 garlic cloves (optional). To cook: 1 T cooking oil; 1 onion, finely diced; 1 t curry powder; 1 t extra-hot chilli powder.

MISPRINT, identified and resolved only by cross-checking a third printing: this page prints '½ dried chilli flakes' WITH NO UNIT, in both fetches. NO SALT is listed either. A Stylist printing of the same version, 5 February 2021, byline 'Zoe says', TWO-PASS on ingredients, supplies both missing pieces — it prints '½ tsp dried chilli flakes' and includes 'sea salt to taste'. The teaspoon unit above therefore comes from that third printing, and the fact that it was missing here is recorded rather than silently filled.
Method as printed: simmer '35–40 minutes until tomato tartness diminishes'.

THE DISAGREEMENT WITH THE 2017 PRINTING, unreconciled, which is why both are published. Fresh tomato: 600 g here against 250 g in 2017. Roasted red bell peppers: 2 here, NONE in 2017. Chilli flakes: ½ teaspoon here against 1 tablespoon in 2017 — a sixfold drop. Salt: omitted on this page, 1 teaspoon in 2017, 'to taste' in the Stylist printing. The tinned-tomato option (400 g) and the tomato purée (30 g) are unchanged. See GHA031.

WHY BOTH ARE PUBLISHED RATHER THAN THE LATER ONE SUPERSEDING THE EARLIER: the roasted peppers change the sauce's character, not just its proportions, and several of this author's other recipes specify a volume of 'uncooked Chalé Sauce' without saying which version. A reader following GHA014 needs to know there are two.

The same sauce appears inline within her peanut sauce page at delicious. magazine (see GHA033) and in Vice, with quantities differing again in each. Those are recorded rather than published separately.
healthBenefits: Roasted red peppers are exceptionally high in vitamin C and carotenoids.
Ginger and garlic contribute anti-inflammatory compounds.
culturalNote: Watching a cookbook author's foundation sauce change between printings is a small window into how recipes actually develop — the roasted peppers were presumably an improvement she made and kept, and the chilli flakes came down because the rest of the heat was doing enough. Neither printing is a correction of the other.
